source: Set the top-left corner of this image on the output canvas. X and Y are whole pixels, starting at zero. Other images keep their current positions. Overlap is allowed here; images imported later are drawn on top. The canvas expands to include all placed images. Crops and sizes stay unchanged.

changes.reason: Use the attested put-in stem iri rather than Japanese ire. The simple past/attributive form is composed from iri-ti and the productive -taru pattern; dictionary iritakii independently supports the irita- stem.

entries.summary: state of having left something inserted

primary_evidence.scope: Past attributives, topic/object syntax, commands, permission, negative existence and purpose patterns; not this exact paragraph.

review_warning: New authoring is not independent acceptance. Re-read the entire candidate, especially the purpose/expansion clause and topical zero-start linkage; do not promote it merely because this local verb correction is supported.

independent_complete_value_review.reviewer: assembly implementation owner; independent of this bounded replacement author
independent_complete_value_review.scope: Reread the complete revised value, not merely the changed stem. Root separately reread all six values and accepted the corrected complete Help.

clauses.corner: Selected image top-left position on output canvas explicitly set.
clauses.coordinates: X and Y whole-number pixel values; following zero-start sentence retains topic.
clauses.other_images: Current positions of other images retained.
clauses.import_order: Later put-in/imported images drawn above earlier ones. iri-taru is a supported past attributive of the native put-in stem.
clauses.canvas: Canvas expands so that every placed image fits; all-object mur(u) and purpose gutu preserve the dependency rather than describing unrelated expansion.
clauses.invariants: Both crop and size remain as they are.

independent_complete_value_review.source_note: NINJAL iri=juN and iritakii support the corrected stem; TUFS 2014 productive past-attributive/purpose grammar. These are component supports for a complete compositional review, not an attested whole UI paragraph.
